recent_facts.fact: When checked on 2026-10-09, the Fox Sports box score showed the game as scheduled with no score yet. It listed kickoff as 'TODAY, 4:00PM' (time zone not given; this is likely 12:00 PM EDT converted to UTC) at ASU Stadium in Montgomery, with Florida A&M at 1-4 and Alabama State at 3-2. Searches turned up no final score.

Because of Tropical Storm Isaias's expected impact on the Gulf Coast, Florida A&M at Alabama State was moved up a day from Saturday, Oct. 10 to Friday, Oct. 9 at noon EDT (11 a.m. CDT). SWAC TV is carrying it.

FAMU comes in at 1-4 (0-1 SWAC). Alabama State is 3-2 (1-1 SWAC) and is playing at home for homecoming. Both teams are starting freshman quarterbacks in place of injured starters: Armond Parker for FAMU and Aaron Frye for Alabama State.
In its most recent game, FAMU lost 40-21 to Alabama A&M on Sept 26, 2026.
Alabama State lost its last game 16-10 to Bethune-Cookman in a Week 5 SWAC game.
Alabama State's 2026 results: beat Southern 30-17 (8/29), beat Lane 34-0 (9/5), lost at Troy 17-34 (9/12), beat Mississippi Valley State 41-15 (9/26), then lost to Bethune-Cookman 16-10.

Through five games FAMU has run for 242 yards (48.4 per game) and 2 TDs, which ranks 12th and last in the SWAC. Its offensive line is short on depth because of injuries. Alabama State's defense has 42 tackles for loss, 12 sacks and 3 INTs. FAMU has 14 sacks and 30 TFLs.
Last season Alabama State won 42-14 at FAMU on Sept 27, 2025.
In 2024 FAMU won 28-13 at Alabama State's homecoming in Montgomery (Oct 5, 2024). In 2022 FAMU won 21-14 (Nov 12, 2022). FAMU leads the all-time series 19-14-2.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $85 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

recent_facts.fact: October 2026 front-month WTI daily highs on this feed (an intraday snapshot for Oct 8): Oct 1 high 93.68, Oct 2 high 93.51, Oct 5 high 91.88, Oct 6 high 90.05, Oct 7 high 90.98, Oct 8 high 93.20. No October session reached $95 on this feed; the October high so far is 93.68.
Recent WTI closes on this feed: Oct 1 92.87, Oct 2 91.11, Oct 5 89.43, Oct 6 89.44, Oct 7 88.28. Oct 8 was trading at 91.08, up 3.17%, after a low of 86.86 on Oct 6.
On Oct 8, WTI futures were up 5% at $92.70 and Brent was up 5.2% at $105.36, after Middle East tensions rose and nine tankers were attacked in and around Hormuz over the past week.

Trading Economics (CFD-based) showed WTI topping $92.6 on Oct 8, its highest in nearly a month, after falling below $89 on Oct 7, its lowest in over a month. It said prices were down about 16% from a September four-month peak as of Oct 7.

The White House reportedly asked the Pentagon for strike options against Iranian targets that could be carried out before the November midterms. The Pentagon reportedly told CENTCOM to finish preparations to resume combat operations in Iran.

Other drivers on Oct 8: tanker attacks in Hormuz last week were the highest weekly level since the war began; about 25% of US Gulf oil output was shut ahead of Tropical Storm Isaias; EIA crude stocks fell by over 3 million barrels; Saudi Arabia cut its official selling prices, and tankers resumed loading in the Gulf.

In September 2026, front-month WTI daily highs ranged widely: 105.63 on Sep 16, 101.69 on Sep 15, 97.22 on Sep 21, 96.78 on Sep 24 and 96.54 on Sep 28. Between Sep 15 and Sep 28, 8 of 10 sessions had highs at or above $95.

WTI closes in 2026 above $100 included Apr 1–2 ($111.54), Apr 29 ($106.88) and Sep 17 ($101.91). Intraday WTI reached nearly $120 in early March. Across the Iran-war period, WTI has repeatedly moved $10+ within a few weeks, e.g. $83.85 on Apr 17 to $106.88 on Apr 29.

Recent swings: WTI jumped 6% to $92.19 on Jul 23 on tanker attacks; it rose from $83.40 (week of Aug 28) to $96.05 on Sep 9 and $101.91 on Sep 17 as US-Iran fighting escalated. Earlier, it fell over 16% in one day on Apr 8 after a ceasefire announcement.

Resolution uses the Pyth 'CLL' feed of the ICE WTI Active Month futures contract, not spot. The EIA Cushing spot series runs well above futures: 97.89 on Oct 2 and 96.24 on Oct 6, against front-month futures closes of 91.11 and 89.44.

recent_facts.fact: After round 1 at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, Eugenio Chacarra, Connor Syme and Grant Forrest led at 5 under (66). Angel Ayora and Sergio García were tied 4th at 4 under, one shot back.

Ayora shot 67 (−4) in round 1, a card that included two eagles and three bogeys. He was the provisional leader during the morning. Afterward he said that if his driver holds up, he will be near the top.

Round 2 is being played today (2026-10-09). I couldn't find any live or completed round 2 scores: the ESPN, Golf Post and Golf Channel leaderboard pages either returned nothing or blocked access. Ayora's standing after round 2 is not verified.
Co-leader Eugenio Chacarra has a foot injury. He said he did not yet know whether he could play round 2 and left open the possibility of withdrawing.

Ayora tees off at 13:50 Spanish time on Friday 9 October from the 1st tee, playing with Ludvig Åberg and Tyrrell Hatton. In round 1, Åberg shot even par and Hatton +5. The tournament has four rounds, 8–11 October, so it finishes Sunday 11 October.

Before the event, Jon Rahm (world #15) was listed as the highest-ranked player in the field, which also included Justin Rose, Shane Lowry, Ludvig Åberg, Tyrrell Hatton, Patrick Reed and defending champion Marco Penge (#53).
Spanish opening-day reports say Jon Rahm did not play because of the birth of his fourth child. Defending champion Marco Penge and Patrick Reed both opened at +2.

Ayora (born 2004) turned pro in 2023. His only professional win is the 2024 Rosa Challenge Tour event. On the DP World Tour he has no wins; his best finishes include T7 at the 2025 Italian Open (he led outright after 36 holes) and T8 at the 2025 DP World Tour Championship. He had ten top-10s in 2025. A single Challenge Tour win is weak evidence of an ability to close out a win.

In the 2026 season (as of July), Ayora had five DP World Tour top-10s, including T5 at the Qatar Masters, T3 at the KLM Open in June and solo 5th at the Open d'Italia in late June. He missed the cut at the Scottish Open, the PGA Championship and The Open, and was 22nd in the Race to Dubai at the time of The Open.
An undated PGA Tour profile gives Ayora's Official World Golf Ranking as 121. This figure may be out of date.
Ayora finished 9th at the 2025 Open de España at the same venue (Club de Campo Villa de Madrid). He is in his second DP World Tour season and has turned down LIV Golf offers.
The question resolves Yes only if Ayora wins the tournament. If he withdraws or does not tee off, the Tournament Winner market resolves No.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Ohio Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 Ohio U.S. Senate special election currently scheduled for November 3, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: The RCP polling average for September 1 to October 5, 2026 has Democrat Sherrod Brown at 47.5% and Republican Sen. Jon Husted at 44.0%, which is Brown +3.5.
A CNN poll of 760 registered voters (Sept 29–Oct 5, MoE ±4.5) had Brown at 49% and Husted at 43%.
The Suffolk/USA Today Ohio poll had Brown at 47% and Husted at 44%, with 6% undecided. The ballot also listed Libertarian William Redpath and No Party candidate Greg Levy.

Marist surveyed 1,298 Ohio registered voters (Sept 24–27, MoE ±3.8). Brown led Husted 51% to 43%, and independents favored Brown 58% to 33%. In the governor's race, Democrat Acton led Republican Ramaswamy 50% to 44%.

Some recent polls show a closer race. InsiderAdvantage (Sept 28–29) had Brown 44%, Husted 43%. Quantus Insights (Sept 21–23) had Brown 48%, Husted 47%. Rasmussen (likely voters) had Brown 46%, Husted 43%, with 7% undecided.
A Portage County bellwether poll (MoE ±5.6) had Husted ahead of Brown 48% to 44%, unlike the statewide polls.

In the 2024 Ohio Senate race, Republican Bernie Moreno beat Brown 50.1% to 46.5% (R+3.6). The final RCP average (Oct 23–Nov 4) was Moreno +1.7, so the polls understated the Republican margin by about 1.9 points. A NYT/Siena poll in late September 2024 had Brown +4.

In 2024, Brown led in several mid-campaign polls, and the race moved toward the Republican over the last weeks. Final individual polls ranged from a tie (Trafalgar) to Moreno +3 (Emerson, AtlasIntel).
NPR calls the race a toss-up that could decide Senate control for Trump's last two years in office. Cook Political Report also rates it a Toss-up.

Brown voted in Franklin County on the first day of early voting. He pointed to voter unhappiness over the war with Iran and over food and diesel prices. Husted has said he would back a federal gas tax holiday.
The Hill reported that Donald Trump is scheduled to hold a rally for Jon Husted in Ohio.

Brown's campaign says national Republicans are spending more than $270 million against him; this is the campaign's own figure. Separately, the crypto super PAC Fairshake reportedly plans to spend at least $30 million opposing Brown.
Ohio early voting runs from Oct 6 to Nov 1, 2026, and the voter registration deadline was Oct 5. The special election is Nov 3, 2026. The searches turned up no scheduled Brown–Husted debate.
Brown raised $7.3M in Q4 2025 and had about $9.9M cash on hand. Husted's two committees raised $1.5M in Q4 and $7.3M across all of 2025.

market.question: US-Iran Hormuz Agreement by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between the United States and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between the United States and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian policies, obligations, or commitments  aimed at permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

Reporters described Brown's status as doubtful. Ferentz said 'it'd be foolish to say that Hank is starting.' Jeremy Hecklinski is taking first-team practice reps, with Jimmy Sullivan as the next backup. Hecklinski's only college stats found were 2-of-2 passing for 8 yards and a 6-yard rushing TD, both in 2025 mop-up duty.

The game is Friday, Oct. 9, 2026, at 9:00 pm ET on FOX, at Alaska Airlines Field at Husky Stadium in Seattle, which is Washington's home field. Iowa is 4-1 and Washington is 3-2 (0-2 Big Ten). One search summary claimed this was Washington's 'third trip to Iowa City'; that conflicts with the venue every source lists.
No. 5 Ohio State beat No. 14 Iowa 31-14 at Kinnick Stadium. Iowa trailed 31-6 before a late touchdown. Julian Sayin threw for 324 yards and 3 TDs, and Brown fumbled on the second play from scrimmage.
Washington lost 25-21 at No. 18 USC on Oct. 3 and 27-24 to Minnesota on Sept. 26. Both conference losses were by 4 points or fewer.

Washington's results: beat Washington State 24-10 (Sept. 6), beat Utah State 16-14 (Sept. 12), beat FCS Eastern Washington 48-16 (Sept. 19), then lost to Minnesota 24-27 and at USC 21-25. The three wins came against non-Big Ten opponents.
Iowa beat Michigan 20-19 the week before the Ohio State game. That is Iowa's only Big Ten win (1-1 in conference).

Iowa's non-conference results: beat Northern Illinois 40-0, beat Iowa State 16-13 on Sept. 12 with a last-second 42-yard field goal, and beat FCS Northern Iowa 55-0 on Sept. 19, when three running backs each ran for 100+ yards.

Washington QB Demond Williams Jr. has 1,327 passing yards and 8 TDs. Iowa's Hank Brown has 832 passing yards and 5 TDs, and Kamari Moulton leads Iowa with 311 rushing yards. Washington is 14th in FBS in turnover margin at +5.

Iowa safety Tyler Brown is 'out for a while' (he has played 2 of 5 games). Backup safety Ty Hudkins is questionable. CB/S Zach Lutmer is good to go, and DB Deshaun Lee expects to play. DB Kyle Gerardy was out against Ohio State, and no update for Washington was found.

This is a Friday night road game at Husky Stadium, kicking off at 6:00 pm PT. Iowa has a bye week afterward, and Washington plays at Purdue on Oct. 16. The Big Ten availability report comes out about two hours before kickoff and will confirm whether Hank Brown plays.

Five players are T7 at -5 (Keith Mitchell, Kristoffer Ventura, Michael Thorbjornsen, Andrew Putnam, David Lipsky). Nico Echavarria, Min Woo Lee, Collin Morikawa, Ryo Hisatsune and Hideki Matsuyama (2021 winner) are at -4. Defending champion Xander Schauffele is at -1, seven shots back.
The field has 72 players and there is no 36-hole cut, so every player plays all four rounds. The course is par 71 at Yokohama Country Club.
The event runs October 8–11, 2026, with a $8,000,000 purse, so three rounds remain (Oct 9–11). Homa's Round 2 tee time is 9:07 a.m. local (8:07 p.m. EDT), paired with Steven Fisk and Kurt Kitayama.

market.question: Will Student List – Students Win win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia – Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
recent_facts.fact: Opposition and independent media accuse Ipsos and Faktor Plus of pro-government bias. A Bureau for Social Research study found that most Serbian pollsters do not disclose weighting or funding. CRTA's July poll left out 12.2% undecided, and an April NSPM scenario poll left out 21% undecided.

RIK accepted 18 lists and 1 was withdrawn. List #1 is 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS, PUPS, SRS, ZS and others; 209,130 signatures). List #3 is 'Student List – Students Are Winning', headed by Ilija Srdanović (69,099 signatures). SPS–JS (Dačić) is running separately as list #2.

Vučić resigned as president on 27 Sep 2026 to lead the SNS list as its prime ministerial candidate. The snap election was announced on 8–9 Sep and set for 25 Oct, more than a year before the regular vote due in late 2027.

Several opposition groups consolidated behind the Student List. The People's Serbia coalition (NPS, NLS, EU) withdrew its list on 22 Sep to back it, after NLS and EU had endorsed it on 15 Sep. PSG left the PES coalition in late September to support the Student List. PES (SSP/SRCE, Tepić/Ponoš) is still running separately as list #9 but has said it will cooperate with the Student List.

In late September, pro-government tabloids ran campaigns against Student List leader Srdanović, which fact-checkers said used AI-manipulated photos. Televised debates are scheduled on RTS, N1, Nova and Radio Belgrade from 29 Sep to 8 Oct.

Vreme reports that polls are dominated by two blocs, 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' and the Student List. A September NSPM survey suggested that Dačić's SPS may struggle to clear the 3% threshold.

The CRTA / Stanford Democracy Action Lab survey (June fieldwork, n=2,324) put the Student List at 44.9% and SNS at 35.7% among decided voters. It was the first published poll to show the Student List ahead.
No Ipsos, CRTA or other poll fielded in October 2026 turned up. The most recent published polls are Faktor Plus (21 Sep) and NSPM (30 Sep, fieldwork early September).

In the December 2023 snap election, preliminary results gave the SNS list 47.95% and Serbia Against Violence 24.32%, with SPS at 6.75%. Ipsos/CeSID exit polls (about 47% vs 23%) were close to the count. Unverified recollection: an SNS-led list has won the most seats in every parliamentary election since 2012 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023), 6 of 6.

All 250 seats are elected by nationwide proportional representation with a 3% threshold. Minority lists, including #4, 5, 6, 10, 14, 15, 17 and 18, are exempt from the threshold. The question resolves on seats won by the ballot-named list, with ties broken by votes.
Election day is 25 Oct 2026, the same day the question closes. RIK (rik.parlament.gov.rs) publishes the preliminary and final results.
